subject: botany
question_text: Give an account of the floral diagram.

verification.note: Chapter 8 is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book pp.21-22), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star rank and NO year citation — so `stars` is 0 and `appearances` is empty by construction, not by omission. Only ONE botany source book is held: there is no TSBIE Basic Learning Material for botany (the copy in hand is physics-only) and no botany board paper in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the back-test against a real paper are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this chapter. This card is NOT-CHECKED — do not read that as checked-and-clean. The mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. BOOK INCONSISTENCY: the book’s printed floral diagram shows a bract at the bottom, but the floral formula printed under it begins "Ebr Ebrl" (ebracteate and ebracteolate, i.e. no bract). A flower drawn with a bract is bracteate (Br). The formula is not reproduced on this card for that reason; the bract is drawn because the book’s own account describes it.

steps.label: What it shows
lines: A floral diagram is a ground plan of a flower,
drawn as a set of circles seen from above.
It shows the number of parts in each whorl,
whether they are free or fused, and how the
whorls are placed with respect to one another.
It is drawn beside the floral formula, which gives
the same information in symbols.
steps.why: A floral diagram and a floral formula carry the same facts in two forms, so saying what the diagram records is the definition.
common_mistakes: Calling it a picture of the flower. It is a plan, not a drawing of the real flower.
Leaving out that it shows the number of parts.
steps.memory_tip: The formula writes the flower in symbols; the diagram draws the same flower in circles.
steps.margin_note: Two or three lines. Say "number, fusion and position".

steps.label: The whorls
lines: Calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium are
drawn in successive circles, from the outside
inwards.
Parts that are fused are joined by a line drawn
between them.
The gynoecium is drawn in the centre, and the
section of the ovary shows the number of locules
and the placentation.
steps.why: The circles run in the same order as the whorls of the real flower, so the outermost circle is always the calyx.
common_mistakes: Drawing the gynoecium on the outside. It is always at the centre.
Drawing only three whorls. All four are shown.
steps.memory_tip: Outside in: calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium. The same order as K, C, A, G in the formula.
steps.margin_note: Name the four whorls in order. That order is the mark.

steps.label: Diagram
steps.why: The account is only convincing with the plan drawn: the dot at the top, the bract at the bottom and four circles between them are exactly what the words describe.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the dot for the mother axis, which fixes the posterior side.
Drawing the whorls as separate flowers instead of as one set of rings.
steps.memory_tip: Dot at the top, bract at the bottom, four rings between them.
steps.margin_note: Draw and label the mother axis, the four whorls and the bract.

steps.label: Mother axis and bract

lines.text: Mother axis at top; bract at bottom

lines: The mother axis is the stem that bears the
flower. It is shown as a dot or small circle at the
top, and that side of the flower is posterior.
The bract is shown at the bottom, and that side
is anterior.
steps.why: Without the dot and the bract there is no way to tell which part of the flower is posterior, so these two marks fix the whole plan.
common_mistakes: Putting the bract at the top and the axis at the bottom.
Calling the axis side anterior. The side towards the mother axis is posterior.
steps.memory_tip: The axis is behind the flower, so the axis side is posterior. The bract is in front, so the bract side is anterior.
steps.margin_note: One boxed line plus the posterior and anterior words.

insider_note: Two of the four marks are for the dot and the bract, not for the rings. Draw them first and label them.
